q: The proxy saw a request, but the same domain was automatically previewed. What should the case report say?
options: The user clicked because the domain appears in the proxy log
The message was delivered to any identity in the DNS record
The preview proves the user's account was not affected
Interaction remains unverified pending attributed evidence
explanation: A request can be automated and needs context before attributing it.

q: What belongs in an executive incident update?
options: A raw unredacted export of every event in the case
Only the internal file hash for the incomplete original message
Business impact, decisions and the next update time
A full list of login failures with no operating implications
explanation: Executives need impact and actionable decisions without unnecessary evidence details.

q: The report says 40 users were compromised based on 40 deliveries. What is the strongest correction?
options: Change the count to 39 to reflect likely duplicate messages
Report delivery count and assess interaction or compromise separately
Assume compromise for any mailbox that has a valid corporate identity
Omit the delivery count until the case is ready for public release
explanation: Evidence of delivery supports a different claim from compromise.

q: What should a technical handoff include alongside the timeline?
options: Source references, scope and open checks
Only the highest incident priority and its colour
A shortened account of whatever arrived first in the team's inbox
The management report without the data behind its conclusions
explanation: The next analyst needs enough detail to reproduce observations and verify actions.

q: A 48.2 MB upload appears in a proxy event. Which update is accurate?
options: The upload confirms exactly 48.2 MB of payroll records were disclosed
The proxy record names the data subject of each file that left the system
The case contains no evidence of data movement because payloads were not logged
The transfer is observed; its contents are unknown
explanation: Byte count and destination identify transfer metadata without naming the content.

q: How should a finding qualified by a narrow search be written?
options: State that the whole organisation has no additional exposure
List the number beside an unqualified incident closure decision
Name the source, search boundary and result
Use only a rewrite of the original alert's severity text
explanation: The search limits constrain what the result can support.

q: An analyst's earlier assessment is disproved by new records. What should the report do?
options: Silently rewrite the earlier judgment in every distributed copy
Retain the earlier version and explain the revision
Discard the new evidence to preserve a consistent timeline
Remove the timestamps so readers cannot see the discrepancy
explanation: Versioning shows what was known and why the conclusion changed.

q: What is a useful role of an evidence appendix?
options: Locate source material and custody references
Publish restricted artifacts in the executive distribution list
Replace the incident action register with file names
Summarise the case's severity in a single colour
explanation: The appendix supports reproducibility and a separate controlled evidence record.

q: A suspected external notification might be required. What should the SOC record?
options: A legal conclusion inferred directly from internal severity
The SOC's final verdict copied from a prior unrelated incident
The technical team's plan to send the report without authorisation
The facts handed to the designated owner and their decision status
explanation: Designated owners determine obligations using evidence and applicable requirements.

q: Which wording clearly marks an assessment?
options: A 48.2 MB transfer was recorded by the proxy at 08:12Z
The gateway accepted the message at the timestamp on the trace
The sequence is consistent with compromise, with stated confidence
The case reference was created by the service desk system
explanation: The phrase indicates an interpretation whose confidence should be stated.

q: Two record sets have different visibility boundaries. How can the report avoid combining their negatives incorrectly?
options: Use the broadest time filter and apply it to all sources implicitly
State each scope and result with its source
State that source diversity proves every kind of activity was covered
Label all missing observations as a single confirmed negative finding
explanation: One source's coverage cannot replace the other's evidence limits.

q: Which report belongs in a restricted case system?
options: The detailed record containing sensitive evidence references
The public-facing message approved for general distribution
An anonymised summary presenting approved aggregate rates
The generic article explaining how to report suspicious mail
explanation: The full case detail requires access appropriate to its contents.

q: A review sees a logon success close in time to an endpoint event, with no shared entity. What should the report do?
options: State each thread was performed by a single attacker because times overlap
Delete the identity record so the endpoint case appears simpler
Combine the two actions into one verified fact without a source
Treat linkage as a hypothesis and assign its verification
explanation: Temporal overlap can justify inquiry without establishing attribution.

q: Why preserve UTC in a case chronology?
options: It makes the user's recollection more precise than the source records
It records when every system ingested the event without extra fields
It gives logs and reviewers a common time reference
It converts observations and inferences into the same kind of evidence
explanation: A consistent time base helps reviewers compare different sources.

q: A report has a distribution marking. What else governs external release?
options: The marking by itself authorises immediate release to anyone
The approved access, sharing and release process
The number of executives who have already opened the document
The recipient's claim that a similar report was shared previously
explanation: Distribution markings do not replace authorization or applicable sharing duties.

q: What does an action register need for follow-up?
options: A decision or status, an owner and a review time
The sender address of every lookalike message in chronological order
An unsigned final report with no remaining actions listed
An internal risk label without the change that was requested
explanation: Action details let readers track what remains and who owns it.

q: A case says an endpoint block is achieved, but the only record is an assigned task. What should change?
options: Keep it complete because an operator was named
Change the scope from endpoint to mail quarantine
Remove the request so the action register contains only closed items
Report the action as pending verification
explanation: Assignment does not provide evidence that the intended protection took effect.

q: What should a peer be able to do with a timeline?
options: Reconstruct an employee's exact intentions from a timestamp alone
Infer the financial loss directly from every ordered event
Trace an observation to its source record
Identify the responsible legal authority from the alert's colour
explanation: Provenance lets a reviewer verify observed facts and their order.

q: Which sentence gives the best actionable bottom line?
options: Something strange happened, and the SOC will check its tools again soon
WS-104 shows suspicious execution; endpoint lead to verify isolation by 09:10Z
Case 41 includes several logs, some of which appear important in isolation
An employee may be involved; update all lists when consensus is reached
explanation: A useful bottom line identifies the risk, owner, decision and timing.

q: Which individual-level detail is usually unnecessary in a metric report?
options: The names associated with individual recipient actions
The measured interval and the definitions of its endpoints
The aggregate number of reports in the period reviewed
The source used to calculate the indicator being reported
explanation: Aggregate reporting can convey process performance without identifying people.

q: The draft calls traffic from a sandbox detonation an observed company endpoint click. What is the correction?
options: Attribute the request to any user who works in the target department
Count both the sandbox and employee as the same user interaction
Remove the sandbox's run identifier after reporting the click
Record the sandbox observation and separate it from device evidence
explanation: The source of activity determines which interaction it can substantiate.

q: What evidence supports the delivery rung most directly?
options: A security team screenshot showing a visually similar message
A user name displayed in the sender's note
A trusted trace showing completed receipt by the mailbox
An endpoint alert that lacks any message context
explanation: Trusted mail disposition can distinguish delivery from rejection or holding.

q: A full report has urgent facts and restricted raw artifacts. How should a wider update be prepared?
options: Attach every artifact so the recipients can draw their own conclusions
Use approved facts with sensitive details omitted and owner review
Send live links and the original artifact across all departments
Replace the evidence with unsupported conclusions to avoid a restriction
explanation: An audience-appropriate derivative can preserve meaning without expanding evidence access.

q: What purpose does a next-update time serve?
options: It sets a clear expectation for new findings or decisions
It proves that response measures will finish by that exact second
It identifies the earliest technical event in the investigation
It substitutes for assigning owners to the open decisions
explanation: A reporting cadence reduces uncertainty while investigation continues.

q: Who should assess an applicable notification obligation?
options: Any analyst who first saw the source event in a dashboard
The sender of the reported email requesting acknowledgment
The operator who ran the last artifact analysis job
The person designated by the organisation's reporting process
explanation: The SOC supplies facts and routes the assessment to the assigned owner.
